propositions.text: The appellant is a citizen of Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The appellant, XXXX XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Tunisia.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the appellant is a citizen of Tunisia.

propositions.text: He fears for his life from C., a radical Islamist who attacked and threatened him for criticizing radical Islam.
propositions.quote: Should he return to Tunisia, he fears for his life at the hands of XXXX XXXX (hereinafter referred to as "C."), a radical Islamist member of the Salafist political party Ennahdha, who attacked and threatened to kill the appellant for criticizing radical Islam.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant fears for his life from C., a radical Islamist who attacked and threatened him for criticizing radical Islam.

propositions.text: The appellant appeals the RPD decision rejecting his refugee claim and argues the RPD erred on internal flight alternative analysis in Sfax and Hammamet.
propositions.quote: He submits that the RPD erred in its analysis of an internal flight alternative (IFA) in Sfax and Hammamet.

propositions.text: He asks the RAD to accept new evidence.
propositions.quote: He also asks the Refugee Appeal Division (RAD) to accept new evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant appeals the RPD decision, arguing error on internal flight alternative and requests RAD to accept new evidence.

propositions.text: The RAD concludes the RPD decision is correct and an internal flight alternative is available in Sfax and Hammamet.
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out below, the RAD concludes that the RPD's decision is correct. An IFA is available to the appellant in Sfax and Hammamet.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD decision is correct and an internal flight alternative is available in Sfax and Hammamet.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal.

propositions.text: The appellant asks the RAD to accept new evidence not presented to the RPD: Exhibit "A" - Statement of source deductions.
propositions.quote: The appellant asks the RAD to accept the following new evidence that was not presented to the RPD: * Exhibit "A" - Statement of source deductions, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX2022.1

paragraphs.summary: The appellant asks the RAD to accept new evidence, Exhibit "A", not presented to the RPD.

propositions.text: To rely on new evidence, appellant must show admissibility under subsection 110(4) IRPA and criteria in Raza and Singh.
propositions.quote: To be able to rely on evidence that was not presented to the RPD, the appellant must demonstrate to the RAD that this evidence is admissible under subsection 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (IRPA) and the criteria in Raza,2 as adapted in Singh3 (Singh/Raza). Exhibit "A" is not admissible as evidence

paragraphs.summary: The court states new evidence must meet subsection 110(4) IRPA and Raza/Singh criteria; Exhibit "A" is not admissible.

propositions.text: Exhibit "A" does not meet any criteria in subsection 110(4) IRPA and is not admissible.
propositions.quote: The RAD concludes that the statement of deductions intended to show the information retained by the Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale [national social security fund] in Tunisia (Exhibit "A") does not meet any of the criteria in subsection 110(4) of the IRPA. Consequently, this document is not admissible as evidence.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds Exhibit "A" does not meet subsection 110(4) IRPA criteria and is inadmissible.

propositions.text: The appellant submits Exhibit "A" is evidence that did not exist at the RPD hearing time.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits that it is evidence that did not exist at the time of the RPD hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits Exhibit "A" did not exist at the time of the RPD hearing.

propositions.text: The RAD rejects that Exhibit "A" is new evidence; the information was available before RPD rejection.
propositions.quote: The RAD rejects this argument. The RAD accepts that the statement in question was issued after the rejection of the claim by the RPD. However, the RAD is of the opinion that evidence to the effect that a taxpayer's address is information held by the Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale in Tunisia is information that was available before the RPD rejected the refugee protection claim.

propositions.text: The appellant did not claim this is a new procedure in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The appellant does not submit that this is a new procedure in Tunisia.

propositions.text: The appellant testified before the RPD that to work in Tunisia he would have to provide his address to the Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, he testified before the RPD that, if he were to return to Tunisia, he would have to work and, to do that, he would have to provide his address to the Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale.4

paragraphs.summary: The RAD rejects the appellant's claim that Exhibit "A" is new evidence, noting the information was available and testified to before the RPD.

propositions.text: The appellant gave no explanation why corroborating evidence was not provided earlier, failing to show it was not reasonably available before RPD rejection.
propositions.quote: The appellant gave no explanation as to why documentary evidence corroborating his testimony could not have been provided to the RPD before the rejection of his refugee protection claim. Consequently, the RAD is of the opinion that he failed to demonstrate that this is information that was not reasonably available before the rejection of the refugee protection claim.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellant failed to explain why corroborating evidence was not provided earlier and was reasonably available before RPD rejection.

propositions.text: The IFA was a determinative issue at the RPD hearing and the appellant was questioned about being tracked in the proposed IFAs.
propositions.quote: With regard to whether this is information that the appellant could reasonably have been expected to have presented to the RPD, the RAD considered that the IFA was a determinative issue at the hearing before the RPD. Furthermore, he was asked about Mr. XXXX ability to track him down in the proposed IFAs.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the IFA was determinative at the RPD hearing and appellant was questioned about tracking in IFAs.

propositions.text: The statement of deductions does not meet any criteria in subsection 110(4) IRPA.
propositions.quote: In light of the above, the RAD is of the opinion that the statement of deductions does not meet any of the criteria in subsection 110(4) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the statement of deductions does not meet subsection 110(4) IRPA criteria.

propositions.text: The statement is not new evidence as appellant testified about it and RPD did not doubt his testimony; it cannot contradict RPD fact findings.
propositions.quote: In addition, the RAD is of the opinion that this is not new evidence. First, the appellant testified about this information before the RPD. Furthermore, the RPD did not doubt the appellant's testimony in this regard. Consequently, the new document cannot be used to contradict a finding of fact by the RPD.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the statement is not new evidence and cannot contradict RPD fact findings.

propositions.text: Although Exhibit "A" is inadmissible, the RAD accepts appellant's uncontradicted testimony that he must provide contact info to work in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: That said, although the statement of deductions is not admissible as evidence, for the purposes of its analysis, considering the appellant's uncontradicted testimony in this regard, the RAD accepts that, if he were to return to Tunisia, he would have to provide his contact information to the Caisse nationale de sécurité sociale in order to be able to work.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD accepts appellant's uncontradicted testimony about providing contact info to work, despite Exhibit "A" inadmissibility.

propositions.text: The appellant submits Exhibit "A" supports a new hearing before the RAD.
propositions.quote: The appellant submits that he is presenting Exhibit "A" in support of a new hearing before the RAD.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits Exhibit "A" supports a new hearing before the RAD.

propositions.text: Under subsection 110(6) IRPA, RAD may hold oral hearing only if certain criteria, including admissible new evidence, are met.
propositions.quote: However, under subsection 110(6) of the IRPA, the RAD may only hold an oral hearing when certain criteria are met, particularly when new evidence is admissible.

paragraphs.summary: The court states RAD may hold oral hearing only if criteria including admissible new evidence are met under subsection 110(6) IRPA.

propositions.text: Since Exhibit "A" is inadmissible, RAD cannot hold an oral hearing under subsection 110(6) IRPA.
propositions.quote: Considering the previous conclusion that Exhibit "A" is not admissible as evidence, the RAD cannot hold an oral hearing pursuant to subsection 110(6) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD cannot hold an oral hearing because Exhibit "A" is inadmissible under subsection 110(6) IRPA.

propositions.text: The RAD applied the correctness standard of review and independently assessed the evidence, including the hearing recording.
propositions.quote: The RAD applied the correctness standard of review.5 The RAD conducted an independent assessment of the evidence, including listening to the recording of the hearing.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD applied correctness standard and independently assessed evidence including hearing recording.

propositions.text: The appellant submits the RPD erred by not separately analyzing the claim under subsection 97(1) IRPA.
propositions.quote: In addition to his arguments regarding the IFA, which will be addressed below, the appellant also submits that the RPD erred by failing to conduct a separate analysis of the claim under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant submits the RPD erred by failing to separately analyze the claim under subsection 97(1) IRPA.

propositions.text: The RAD rejects the appellant's argument about the RPD's analysis.
propositions.quote: The RAD rejects this argument.

propositions.text: The RPD conducted an analysis under both section 96 and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.
propositions.quote: the RPD conducted an analysis of the claim under both section 96 of the IRPA and subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD rejects the appellant's argument and notes the RPD analyzed the claim under sections 96 and 97(1) of the IRPA.

propositions.text: The appellant failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution on Convention grounds or a risk under subsection 97(1) if returned to Tunisia.
propositions.quote: the appellant has failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution on one of the five Convention grounds or, on a balance or probabilities, that he would be subjected personally to a danger of torture, to a risk to his life, or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, under subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, if he were to return to Tunisia.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err in its analysis of the internal flight alternative in Sfax and Hammamet.
propositions.quote: The Refugee Protection Division did not err in its analysis of an internal flight alternative in Sfax and Hammamet

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellant failed to prove persecution or risk under IRPA and that the RPD did not err on internal flight alternative analysis.

propositions.text: The internal flight alternative (IFA) determination is based on a two-pronged test.
propositions.quote: The IFA determination is based on a two-pronged test.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD states the IFA determination uses a two-pronged test.

propositions.text: First prong: claimants must establish serious possibility of persecution or risk under subsection 97(1) in the proposed IFAs.
propositions.quote: For the first prong, refugee protection claimants must establish that there is a serious possibility of persecution or, on a balance of probabilities, a risk within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA in the proposed IFAs.

paragraphs.summary: The first prong requires claimants to prove serious possibility of persecution or risk under subsection 97(1) in proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: Second prong: claimants must establish it would be objectively unreasonable to seek refuge in the proposed IFAs.
propositions.quote: For the second prong, refugee protection claimants must establish that it would be objectively unreasonable for them to seek refuge in the proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: The appellant failed to establish a prospective risk in Sfax and Hammamet.
propositions.quote: The appellant failed to establish that there is a prospective risk in Sfax and Hammamet

paragraphs.summary: The second prong requires proving unreasonableness to seek refuge in IFAs; appellant failed to prove risk in Sfax and Hammamet.

propositions.text: The RPD did not err in concluding appellant failed to establish serious possibility of persecution or risk in Sfax and Hammamet under subsection 97(1).
propositions.quote: the RPD did not err in concluding that the appellant had failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution in Sfax and Hammamet or, on a balance of probabilities, that he would be subjected personally to a risk there within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD agrees the RPD did not err in finding no serious possibility of persecution or risk in Sfax and Hammamet.

propositions.text: The RPD's conclusions are based on assumptions and conjecture, not clear evidence.
propositions.quote: the appellant submits that several of the conclusions or inferences drawn by the RPD are based more on assumptions and conjecture, rather than on clear conclusions based on the evidence.

propositions.text: The RPD made sweeping conclusions and minimized C.'s role and ability to track appellant in IFAs.
propositions.quote: He adds that the RPD made a number of sweeping conclusions. He submits that the RPD minimized the role played, as well as C.'s motivation and ability to track him down in the proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: Since RPD found appellant credible on allegations, he is credible on lack of IFA.
propositions.quote: He adds that since the RPD found him credible with respect to his allegations, he is also credible with respect to the lack of an IFA.

propositions.text: The RPD erred by not addressing C.'s ability to track appellant anywhere in Tunisia via social security information.
propositions.quote: He adds that the RPD erred by failing to address C.'s ability to track him down anywhere in Tunisia, through the information he has to disclose to social security.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD's conclusions are assumptions, minimized C.'s role, and erred by not addressing C.'s tracking ability.

propositions.text: The RAD disagrees with appellant's arguments and notes appellant bears burden to prove agent of persecution's motivation to track him in IFAs.
propositions.quote: The RAD disagrees with the appellant's arguments. It is incumbent on me to note that the appellant has the burden of establishing that his agent of persecution would have the interest and motivation to track him down in the proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: The RAD agrees with RPD that appellant failed to discharge burden to prove motivation to track him.
propositions.quote: However, like the RPD, the RAD is of the opinion that he failed to discharge this burden.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD rejects appellant's arguments and finds he failed to prove C.'s motivation to track him in IFAs.

propositions.text: Appellant met C. three times at same café during 2014-2015 stay in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The appellant's testimony revealed that during his stay in Tunisia from XXXX 2014 to XXXX 2015, he met C. three times, always at the same café.

propositions.text: Appellant's friend stated appellant ran into C. in 2022 at same neighbourhood café.
propositions.quote: according to the written statement of his friend XXXX, he also ran into C. in XXXX 2022, again at the same neighbourhood café.

propositions.text: RAD finds appellant failed to prove meetings with C. were more than chance encounters.
propositions.quote: the RAD is of the opinion that the appellant failed to establish that these meetings with C. were anything more than chance encounters.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds appellant's meetings with C. at the same café were chance encounters, not evidence of tracking.

propositions.text: C. lives in same neighbourhood as appellant's parents; café is 10-minute walk from parents' home.
propositions.quote: According to the appellant's testimony, C. lives in the same neighbourhood as his parents. The café where the altercations with C. occurred is about a ten-minute walk from the appellant's parent's home.

propositions.text: In past eight years, no one in appellant's family or friends approached by C. except 2022 café encounter.
propositions.quote: over the past eight years, neither his family nor his friends in the neighbourhood have been approached by C., other than the encounter with XXXX at the café in XXXX 2022.

propositions.text: Appellant stated he did not know if C. tried to find him and that C. has problem only with appellant.
propositions.quote: he did not know whether C. had tried to find him and that, furthermore, he is the one that C. has a problem with because he stood up to him.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD notes C. lives near appellant's family; no contact with family or friends except one café encounter; appellant unsure if C. tried to find him.

propositions.text: Appellant's father and two friends went to police and were willing to testify against C.
propositions.quote: the appellant's father and the appellant's two friends went to the police station with him. His friends were willing to testify against C.

propositions.text: RAD accepts C. interested only in appellant, not family or friends, who have not been approached except one café encounter.
propositions.quote: the RAD accepts that C. would only be interested in the appellant and not his parents or friends. That said, they have never been approached by C. in all these years, other than a chance encounter with XXXX at the neighbourhood café in XXXX 2022

propositions.text: Appellant failed to prove C. is actively looking for him or motivated to track him in IFAs.
propositions.quote: the RAD is of the opinion that the appellant has failed to establish that C. is actively looking for him or that he would have the interest or motivation to track him down in the proposed IFAs.

propositions.text: Risk from C. likely limited to neighbourhood where meetings occurred.
propositions.quote: the RAD is of the opinion that the appellant has failed to establish that the risk he would face at the hands of C. would extend beyond the neighbourhood in question.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds C. only interested in appellant, not family or friends, and risk from C. does not extend beyond the neighbourhood.

propositions.text: Appellant failed to prove C.'s ability to find him in Sfax or Hammamet.
propositions.quote: With regard to C.'s ability to find him in Sfax or Hammamet, the RAD is of the opinion that the appellant failed to establish this.

propositions.text: Appellant would have to disclose contact info to social security if returned to Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The RAD accepts that the appellant would have to disclose his contact information to social security if he were to return to Tunisia.

propositions.text: Appellant stated C. is Ennahdha party member and could access his info.
propositions.quote: At the RPD hearing, the appellant stated that since C. is a member of the Ennahdha political party, he could have access to his information.

propositions.text: Appellant did not provide evidence of C.'s role or influence in Ennahdha party.
propositions.quote: the appellant did not provide any evidence regarding C.'s role in that party or the influence he may have in the party.

propositions.text: Appellant admitted not knowing C.'s role in party and not trying to find out.
propositions.quote: the appellant admitted that he did not know what C.'s role was in the party and had not tried to find out about this role.

propositions.text: Appellant failed to prove C. could access his info via party membership or motivation to track him.
propositions.quote: the appellant has failed to establish that C. could have access to his personal information because of his membership in the Ennahdha political party. That said, even if C. was able to access such information, as previously stated, the appellant has failed to establish that C. has the motivation to take such steps to try to find him.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds appellant failed to prove C.'s ability or motivation to find him via social security or party membership.

propositions.text: Appellant does not contest RPD's conclusion on risk from religious extremists as non-practising Muslim.
propositions.quote: the appellant does not contest the RPD's conclusion that he failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution or, on a balance of probabilities, a risk within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA on this basis.

propositions.text: RAD sees no error and agrees with RPD's conclusion on this risk.
propositions.quote: The RAD sees no error and agrees with this conclusion.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant does not contest, and the RAD agrees with, the RPD's conclusion on no risk from religious extremists.

propositions.text: RAD concludes appellant failed to establish serious possibility of persecution or risk in Sfax or Hammamet under subsection 97(1).
propositions.quote: the RAD concludes that the appellant has failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution or, on a balance of probabilities, a risk within the meaning of subsection 97(1) of the IRPA in Sfax or Hammamet.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes appellant failed to prove persecution or risk in Sfax or Hammamet under subsection 97(1).

propositions.text: RAD agrees RPD did not err in concluding appellant failed to prove it would be unreasonable to seek refuge in Sfax or Hammamet.
propositions.quote: The RAD is of the opinion that the RPD did not err in concluding that the appellant failed to establish that it would be unreasonable for him to seek refuge in Sfax or Hammamet.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds no error in RPD's conclusion that seeking refuge in Sfax or Hammamet is not unreasonable.

propositions.text: Appellant cites case law that IFA must be realistic and claimant cannot face great danger or undue hardship in reaching or staying there.
propositions.quote: Without any specific argument, the appellant cites case law stating that the IFA must be a realistic, attainable option, and the claimant cannot be required to encounter great physical danger or to undergo undue hardship in travelling there or in staying there.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant cites case law that IFA must be realistic and not involve great danger or undue hardship.

propositions.text: Threshold to show IFA is unreasonable is very high; conditions must risk claimant's life or safety.
propositions.quote: The threshold for showing that an IFA is unreasonable is very high. The conditions in the IFA must be such that the refugee protection claimant's life or safety would be at risk.

paragraphs.summary: The law requires a high threshold to prove an IFA is unreasonable, needing risk to life or safety.

propositions.text: At RPD hearing, appellant said he would not have problems settling, working, or living in proposed IFAs besides fear of being found by C.
propositions.quote: At the RPD hearing, besides his fear of being found by C., the appellant stated that he would not experience any problems with settling in the proposed IFAs, and working and living there.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant testified he would have no problems settling or working in IFAs except fear of being found by C.

propositions.text: Appellant is 31, speaks French, English, Arabic; Arabic official language, French used in commerce.
propositions.quote: The appellant is a young 31-year-old man who speaks French, English and Arabic. Arabic is the country's official language and French is used in commerce.

propositions.text: Appellant pursued university studies and held various jobs in Canada in XXXX industry, which he could do in Tunisia.
propositions.quote: The appellant has pursued university studies. In Canada, he has held various jobs in the XXXX XXXX industry, which he could also do in Tunisia.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant is young, multilingual, educated, and has work experience transferable to Tunisia.

propositions.text: RAD concludes appellant failed to prove he could not settle, support himself, find accommodation, and live safely in Sfax or Hammamet.
propositions.quote: the RAD concludes that the appellant has failed to establish that he could not settle in Sfax or Hammamet, support himself, find accommodations and live there safely.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes appellant failed to prove inability to settle, support himself, or live safely in Sfax or Hammamet.

propositions.text: The RAD concludes the RPD's decision is correct.
propositions.quote: the RAD concludes that the RPD's decision is correct.

propositions.text: The appellant failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution on one of the five Convention grounds.
propositions.quote: The appellant has failed to establish a serious possibility of persecution on one of the five Convention grounds

propositions.text: The appellant failed to prove on a balance of probabilities that he would face danger of torture, risk to life, or cruel and unusual treatment if returned to Tunisia.
propositions.quote: or, on a balance of probabilities, that he would be subjected personally to a danger of torture, to a risk to his life, or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment, pursuant to subsection 97(1) of the IRPA, if he were to return to Tunisia.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD decision is correct; the appellant failed to prove persecution or risk of torture, death, or cruel treatment if returned to Tunisia.

propositions.text: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the determination of the RPD that XXXX XXXX XXXX is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of section 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal and confirms the RPD's decision that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.
